claim: Over 1.6 million Americans suffer from significant tricuspid valve leakage.
source: Over 1.6 million Americans suffer from significant tricuspid valve leakage.
evidence: This is a factual statement about disease prevalence that is presented in the abstract without direct citation in this sentence, though it is cited elsewhere in the manuscript.

claim: In most cases of tricuspid valve leakage, this leakage is designated as secondary.
source: In most cases this leakage is designated as secondary.
evidence: This statement about disease classification is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: In secondary tricuspid regurgitation, valve dysfunction is assumed to be due to valve-extrinsic factors.
source: Thus, valve dysfunction is assumed to be due to valve-extrinsic factors.
evidence: This describes the prevailing clinical paradigm about secondary TR.

claim: The tricuspid valve maladapts in disease, rendering the valve at least partially culpable for its dysfunction.
source: We challenge this paradigm and hypothesize that the tricuspid valve maladapts in those patients rendering the valve at least partially culpable for its dysfunction.
evidence: This is the central hypothesis of the study, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Biventricular heart failure in sheep leads to tricuspid valve leakage.
source: To this end, we induced biventricular heart failure in sheep that developed tricuspid valve leakage.
evidence: This describes the experimental model used in the study.

claim: In sheep with biventricular heart failure, the anterior tricuspid valve leaflets show alterations on the protein and cell-level.
source: We demonstrated alterations on the protein and cell-level, leading to tissue growth, thickening, and stiffening.
evidence: This summarizes findings from proteomics and immunohistochemistry experiments.

claim: Protein and cell-level alterations in diseased tricuspid valve leaflets lead to tissue growth, thickening, and stiffening.
source: We demonstrated alterations on the protein and cell-level, leading to tissue growth, thickening, and stiffening.
evidence: This causal relationship is inferred from the multi-scale experimental observations.

claim: Moderate to severe TR affects more than 1.6 million Americans.
source: Moderate to severe TR affects more than 1.6 million Americans and is an independent predictor of mortality (Mangieri et al., 2017; Taramasso et al., 2012; Nath et al., 2004).
evidence: This prevalence statistic is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Tricuspid regurgitation is an independent predictor of mortality.
source: Moderate to severe TR affects more than 1.6 million Americans and is an independent predictor of mortality (Mangieri et al., 2017; Taramasso et al., 2012; Nath et al., 2004).
evidence: This clinical outcome is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In 85% of severe TR cases, TR is considered functional or secondary to right ventricular remodeling and left-sided heart disease.
source: In 85% of severe cases, TR is considered functional or secondary to right ventricular remodeling and left-sided heart disease (Mangieri et al., 2017; Dreyfus et al., 2015; Rogers and Bolling, 2009).
evidence: This classification statistic is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Tricuspid annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement are believed to circumferentially strain and tether the valve's leaflets, preventing proper leaflet coaptation.
source: Here, resultant tricuspid annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement are believed to circumferentially strain and tether the valve's leaflets, respectively, preventing proper leaflet coaptation (Sun and O'Gara, 2017; Spinner et al., 2012).
evidence: This mechanistic explanation is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In functional TR, the valve itself is considered structurally and mechanically intact and healthy.
source: In other words, it is believed that constraints from valve-extrinsic conditions render the valve dysfunctional, while the valve itself is considered structurally and mechanically intact and healthy (Meador et al., 2018; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the traditional clinical paradigm, supported by citations.

claim: TR was historically not treated assuming that it would resolve following treatment of left-sided heart disease.
source: In fact, TR was historically not treated assuming that it would resolve following treatment of left-sided heart disease (Braunwald et al., 1967).
evidence: This historical clinical practice is supported by a citation.

claim: Repair failure rates for tricuspid regurgitation are as high as 10–30%.
source: Despite decades of experience with these devices and techniques, repair failure rates are still as high as 10–30% (Pfannmüller et al., 2012).
evidence: This clinical outcome statistic is supported by a citation.

claim: Mitral valve leaflets grow and remodel in functional mitral regurgitation.
source: Our group and others have shown that the mitral valve leaflets grow and remodel in functional mitral regurgitation (Rausch et al., 2012; Dal-Bianco et al., 2009; Stephens et al., 2009; Grande-Allen et al., 2005a).
evidence: This finding about mitral valve adaptation is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Leaflet growth in the mitral valve may be beneficial by increasing the coaptation area.
source: While leaflet growth, that is adaptation, in the mitral valve may be beneficial by increasing the coaptation area, (Beaudoin et al., 2013; Dal-Bianco and Levine, 2015) concomitant leaflet fibrosis, that is maladaptation, may stiffen the valve and thus impede proper kinematics and coaptation (Grande-Allen et al., 2005b).
evidence: This functional consequence is supported by citations.

claim: Concomitant leaflet fibrosis in the mitral valve may stiffen the valve and thus impede proper kinematics and coaptation.
source: While leaflet growth, that is adaptation, in the mitral valve may be beneficial by increasing the coaptation area, (Beaudoin et al., 2013; Dal-Bianco and Levine, 2015) concomitant leaflet fibrosis, that is maladaptation, may stiffen the valve and thus impede proper kinematics and coaptation (Grande-Allen et al., 2005b).
evidence: This functional consequence is supported by a citation.

claim: The maladaptive, fibrotic response of mitral valve leaflets may be pharmacologically reduced without reducing their adaptive ability to grow.
source: Fortunately, Levine and co-workers have demonstrated that the maladaptive, fibrotic response of the leaflets may be pharmacologically reduced without reducing their adaptive ability to grow (Bartko et al., 2017).
evidence: This therapeutic finding is supported by a citation.

claim: The tricuspid valve has been dubbed the 'forgotten valve'.
source: Similar research on the tricuspid valve is nearly absent, so much so that it has been dubbed the 'forgotten valve' (Stephens and Borger, 2014).
evidence: This characterization is supported by a citation.

claim: Leaflets of patients with pulmonary hypertension may increase in area.
source: Although a first study in humans demonstrated that leaflets of patients with pulmonary hypertension may increase in area, it remains unknown whether tricuspid valve leaflets similarly maladapt during functional TR (Afilalo et al., 2015).
evidence: This human study finding is supported by a citation.

claim: 17 tricuspid valves were successfully isolated from control (CTL) sheep.
source: We successfully isolated 17 tricuspid valves from control (CTL) sheep and 33 tricuspid valves from sheep that underwent 19 ± 6 days of rapid pacing to induce biventricular heart failure (TIC).
evidence: This describes the experimental sample size.

claim: 33 tricuspid valves were successfully isolated from sheep that underwent 19 ± 6 days of rapid pacing to induce biventricular heart failure (TIC).
source: We successfully isolated 17 tricuspid valves from control (CTL) sheep and 33 tricuspid valves from sheep that underwent 19 ± 6 days of rapid pacing to induce biventricular heart failure (TIC).
evidence: This describes the experimental sample size and pacing duration.

claim: The anterior leaflet has the largest major cusp of the three tricuspid valve leaflets.
source: We included only anterior tricuspid valve leaflets in our study because the anterior leaflet has the largest major cusp of the three leaflets which allowed us to conduct all (or most) of our analyses on one and the same tissue.
evidence: This anatomical fact is stated as justification for the experimental design.

claim: The anterior leaflet is suspected to maladapt the most of the three leaflets due to its tethering to the remodeling right ventricular free wall.
source: Furthermore, because of its tethering to the remodeling right ventricular free wall we suspected that the anterior leaflet also maladapts the most of the three leaflets.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on anatomical reasoning.

claim: TIC subjects had significant biventricular ejection fraction reduction.
source: Echocardiographic data and hemodynamic data of the animals revealed significant parameter changes in TIC subjects consistent with clinical biventricular dysfunction and functional tricuspid valve regurgitation (Table 1). Most notably, we observed that TIC subjects had significant biventricular ejection fraction reduction, biventricular remodeling, tricuspid valve annular dilation, and increased TR severity.
evidence: This finding is supported by data presented in Table 1.

claim: TIC subjects had biventricular remodeling.
source: Most notably, we observed that TIC subjects had significant biventricular ejection fraction reduction, biventricular remodeling, tricuspid valve annular dilation, and increased TR severity.
evidence: This finding is supported by data presented in Table 1.

claim: TIC subjects had tricuspid valve annular dilation.
source: Most notably, we observed that TIC subjects had significant biventricular ejection fraction reduction, biventricular remodeling, tricuspid valve annular dilation, and increased TR severity.
evidence: This finding is supported by data presented in Table 1.

claim: TIC subjects had increased TR severity.
source: Most notably, we observed that TIC subjects had significant biventricular ejection fraction reduction, biventricular remodeling, tricuspid valve annular dilation, and increased TR severity.
evidence: This finding is supported by data presented in Table 1.

claim: TIC anterior leaflet areas were 130% larger when compared to CTL anterior leaflets.
source: In summary, TIC anterior leaflet areas were 130% larger when compared to CTL anterior leaflets, ostensibly driven by an increase in leaflet width.
evidence: This finding is supported by morphological measurements presented in Figure 1.

claim: There was a significant increase of approximately 130% in anterior leaflet area for TIC animals compared to CTL animals (p=0.002).
source: However, in our analysis we found a significant increase of approximately 130% in anterior leaflet area for TIC animals compared to CTL animals (p=0.002, Figure 1b).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The increase in anterior leaflet area appeared to be driven by a significant increase in width (p=0.023).
source: These increases in area appeared to be driven by a significant increase in width (p=0.023), and a near significant increase in height (p=0.070) (Figure 1c–d).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by data shown in Figures 1c-d.

claim: There was a near significant increase in anterior leaflet height (p=0.070).
source: These increases in area appeared to be driven by a significant increase in width (p=0.023), and a near significant increase in height (p=0.070) (Figure 1c–d).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by data shown in Figures 1c-d.

claim: Anterior leaflet areas showed no correlation with animal weight in either CTL or TIC animal groups.
source: Furthermore, the anterior leaflet areas showed no correlation with animal weight in either animal groups (CTL: r = 0.239, p = 0.253, TIC: r = 0.077, p = 0.349) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets were 140% thicker when compared to CTL anterior leaflets.
source: In summary, TIC anterior leaflets were 140% thicker when compared to CTL anterior leaflets, mostly driven by increases in the free edge thickness.
evidence: This finding is supported by thickness measurements presented in Figure 2.

claim: The mean thickness of all anterior leaflets decreased from the near-annulus region (thickest) to the free edge (thinnest) in both TIC and CTL animals.
source: In TIC and CTL animals, the mean thickness of all anterior leaflets decreased from the near-annulus region (thickest) to the free edge (thinnest) (Figure 2b).
evidence: This finding is supported by thickness profile data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The mean thickness of TIC anterior leaflets was consistently larger than CTL anterior leaflets in all three regions.
source: Furthermore, the mean thickness of TIC anterior leaflets was consistently larger than CTL anterior leaflets in all three regions.
evidence: This finding is supported by thickness data shown in Figure 2.

claim: There was a significant increase (140%) in TIC anterior leaflet thickness (p=0.006).
source: When summarized into a single average thickness, we found a significant increase (140%) in TIC anterior leaflet thickness (p=0.006, Figure 2c).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The increases in thickness were most strongly driven by a significant increase in the free edge region (p=0.003).
source: When analyzed by region, the increases in thickness were most strongly driven by a significant increase in the free edge region (p=0.003, Figure 2d).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by regional data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: 247 differentially expressed proteins were identified between CTL and TIC anterior leaflets.
source: We utilized proteomics to survey protein-level expression within the TIC anterior leaflets to infer which biological processes were up- or down-regulated in these tissues. To this end, we successfully identified 247 differentially expressed proteins between CTL and TIC anterior leaflets (Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: This finding is supported by proteomic analysis data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets overexpressed metabolic proteins compared to CTL.
source: Compared to CTL, TIC anterior leaflets overexpressed metabolic proteins (ENO1, ESD, ALDOA, ALDOC, ASPH, UGP2, AK1, PGK1, PGK2, PKM, LDHA, PGD, among others), serpins (A1, A5, C1, D1, and others), apolipoproteins (A1 and B), proteins related to matrix remodeling, such as COL6A3, which is tied to the alpha-chain of a type VI collagen, and FN1, GPC4, and PGLYRP1, all proteins involved in synthesis and regulation of glycans.
evidence: This finding is based on proteomic analysis.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets overexpressed serpins compared to CTL.
source: Compared to CTL, TIC anterior leaflets overexpressed metabolic proteins (ENO1, ESD, ALDOA, ALDOC, ASPH, UGP2, AK1, PGK1, PGK2, PKM, LDHA, PGD, among others), serpins (A1, A5, C1, D1, and others), apolipoproteins (A1 and B), proteins related to matrix remodeling, such as COL6A3, which is tied to the alpha-chain of a type VI collagen, and FN1, GPC4, and PGLYRP1, all proteins involved in synthesis and regulation of glycans.
evidence: This finding is based on proteomic analysis.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets overexpressed apolipoproteins compared to CTL.
source: Compared to CTL, TIC anterior leaflets overexpressed metabolic proteins (ENO1, ESD, ALDOA, ALDOC, ASPH, UGP2, AK1, PGK1, PGK2, PKM, LDHA, PGD, among others), serpins (A1, A5, C1, D1, and others), apolipoproteins (A1 and B), proteins related to matrix remodeling, such as COL6A3, which is tied to the alpha-chain of a type VI collagen, and FN1, GPC4, and PGLYRP1, all proteins involved in synthesis and regulation of glycans.
evidence: This finding is based on proteomic analysis.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets showed upregulation of proteins related to matrix remodeling.
source: Compared to CTL, TIC anterior leaflets overexpressed metabolic proteins (ENO1, ESD, ALDOA, ALDOC, ASPH, UGP2, AK1, PGK1, PGK2, PKM, LDHA, PGD, among others), serpins (A1, A5, C1, D1, and others), apolipoproteins (A1 and B), proteins related to matrix remodeling, such as COL6A3, which is tied to the alpha-chain of a type VI collagen, and FN1, GPC4, and PGLYRP1, all proteins involved in synthesis and regulation of glycans.
evidence: This finding is based on proteomic analysis.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets showed upregulation of specific proteins related to the mesenchymal phenotype.
source: Additionally, we found upregulation in specific proteins related to the mesenchymal phenotype, for example CD14, CD163, FERMT2, PLS3, and S100A1.
evidence: This finding is based on proteomic analysis.

claim: Coagulation factor F9 was highly upregulated in TIC anterior leaflets.
source: Finally, we found that coagulation factor F9 was highly upregulated, along with a number of complement proteins (C2, C5, C6, and others), indicating the increased production of pro-inflammatory mediators downstream.
evidence: This finding is based on proteomic analysis.

claim: A number of complement proteins were upregulated in TIC anterior leaflets, indicating increased production of pro-inflammatory mediators downstream.
source: Finally, we found that coagulation factor F9 was highly upregulated, along with a number of complement proteins (C2, C5, C6, and others), indicating the increased production of pro-inflammatory mediators downstream.
evidence: This finding is based on proteomic analysis and inference about downstream effects.

claim: The 247 differentially expressed proteins most often belonged to protein classes of metabolite interconversion enzymes, protein binding modulators, and protein modifying enzymes.
source: We found that these 247 differentially expressed proteins most often belonged to protein classes of metabolite interconversion enzymes, protein binding modulators, and protein modifying enzymes.
evidence: This classification is based on gene ontology analysis of proteomic data.

claim: The 247 differentially expressed proteins were most associated with the molecular functions of catalytic, binding, and regulatory activity.
source: Furthermore, these 247 proteins were most associated with the molecular functions of catalytic, binding, and regulatory activity.
evidence: This classification is based on gene ontology analysis of proteomic data.

claim: The most common cell component for the 247 differentially expressed proteins were organelles, protein complexes, or membranes.
source: The 247 proteins' most common cell component were organelles, protein complexes, or membranes.
evidence: This classification is based on gene ontology analysis of proteomic data.

claim: The most common biological processes for the 247 differentially expressed proteins were metabolic, biological regulation or biogenesis.
source: Finally, the most common biological processes for these 247 proteins were metabolic, biological regulation or biogenesis (e.g., histones, ribosomal, and membrane proteins).
evidence: This classification is based on gene ontology analysis of proteomic data.

claim: There was an increase in TIC αSMA expression, mostly in the atrialis of near-annulus and belly regions.
source: We found an increase in TIC αSMA expression, indicative of cellular activation, mostly in the atrialis of near-annulus and belly regions (Figure 3a).
evidence: This finding is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Increased αSMA expression is indicative of cellular activation.
source: We found an increase in TIC αSMA expression, indicative of cellular activation, mostly in the atrialis of near-annulus and belly regions (Figure 3a).
evidence: This interpretation is based on established knowledge about αSMA as a marker.

claim: Ki67 was increased for TIC in the atrialis of the belly region and in much of the free edge region.
source: Furthermore, Ki67, a marker for cell proliferation, was increased for TIC in the atrialis of the belly region and in much of the free edge region (Figure 3b).
evidence: This finding is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Ki67 is a marker for cell proliferation.
source: Furthermore, Ki67, a marker for cell proliferation, was increased for TIC in the atrialis of the belly region and in much of the free edge region (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Ki67 marker.

claim: Only marginal changes in TIC cell nuclei density were observed in the near-annulus (increased) and free edge (decreased) regions.
source: However, we observed only marginal changes in TIC cell nuclei density in the near-annulus (increased) and free edge (decreased) regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: MMP13 was widely increased for TIC in both near-annulus and belly regions.
source: Additionally, MMP13, a collagenase, was widely increased for TIC in both near-annulus and belly regions (Figure 3c).
evidence: This finding is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: MMP13 is a collagenase.
source: Additionally, MMP13, a collagenase, was widely increased for TIC in both near-annulus and belly regions (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is established knowledge about MMP13.

claim: TGF-β1 increased primarily in the belly region of TIC samples.
source: Lastly, TGF-β1 also increased primarily in the belly region of TIC samples (Figure 3d).
evidence: This finding is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: CTL tissues also expressed remodeling markers (αSMA, Ki67, MMP13, TGF-β1), albeit to a lesser degree, likely suggesting their involvement in maintaining tissue homeostasis.
source: It should be noted that CTL tissues also expressed these markers, albeit to a lesser degree, likely suggesting their involvement in maintaining tissue homeostasis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of marker expression in control tissues.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets had 140% more collagen than CTL anterior leaflets.
source: In summary, TIC anterior leaflets had 140% more collagen than CTL anterior leaflets, mostly driven by increases in the free edge and near-annulus content.
evidence: This finding is supported by quantitative collagen assay data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Collagen content decreased from the near-annulus region to the free edge in both CTL and TIC groups.
source: In both groups, we found collagen content decreased from the near-annulus region to the free edge (Figure 4a).
evidence: This finding is supported by regional collagen data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The mean collagen content was larger in TIC subjects than in CTL subjects in all three regions.
source: Importantly, in all three regions, the mean collagen content was larger in TIC subjects than in CTL subjects.
evidence: This finding is supported by collagen data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The strongest collagen increase was in the free edge region (~150%, p=0.006).
source: The strongest increase was in the free edge region (~150%, p=0.006) and the near-annulus region (~135%, p=0.023), but we failed to find a significant increase in the belly region (~125%, p=0.058).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by regional collagen data shown in Figure 4.

claim: There was a significant collagen increase in the near-annulus region (~135%, p=0.023).
source: The strongest increase was in the free edge region (~150%, p=0.006) and the near-annulus region (~135%, p=0.023), but we failed to find a significant increase in the belly region (~125%, p=0.058).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by regional collagen data shown in Figure 4.

claim: No significant increase in collagen was found in the belly region (~125%, p=0.058).
source: The strongest increase was in the free edge region (~150%, p=0.006) and the near-annulus region (~135%, p=0.023), but we failed to find a significant increase in the belly region (~125%, p=0.058).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by regional collagen data shown in Figure 4.

claim: When all regions were pooled within subjects, there was a significant 140% increase in collagen content in TIC anterior leaflets (p=0.016).
source: When we pooled all regions within subjects, we found a significant 140% increase in collagen content in TIC anterior leaflets (p=0.016, Figure 4b).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by pooled collagen data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Collagen content showed a strong positive (r = 0.650) and significant (p=0.015) correlation with TR severity.
source: We also tested if collagen content would positively correlate with TR severity, as collagen may stiffen and reduce the leaflet's range of motion. Here, we found a strong positive (r = 0.650) and significant (p=0.015) correlation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by correlation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Collagen may stiffen and reduce the leaflet's range of motion.
source: We also tested if collagen content would positively correlate with TR severity, as collagen may stiffen and reduce the leaflet's range of motion.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on established knowledge about collagen's mechanical properties.

claim: All tissues exhibited classic J-shaped loading curves under planar biaxial tension, consistent with other biological collagenous tissues.
source: Under this loading, all tissues exhibited classic J-shaped loading curves, consistent with other biological collagenous tissues (Figure 5a; Sacks, 2000).
evidence: This finding is supported by mechanical testing data shown in Figure 5a and comparison to literature.

claim: The transition stretches and degrees of anisotropy of the loading curves remained mostly consistent between CTL and TIC subjects.
source: In detail, the transition stretches and degrees of anisotropy of the curves remained mostly consistent between CTL and TIC subjects, overall behaving stiffer in the circumferential direction than in the radial direction (i.e., degree of anisotropy <1) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is supported by mechanical data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Anterior leaflets overall behaved stiffer in the circumferential direction than in the radial direction (i.e., degree of anisotropy <1).
source: In detail, the transition stretches and degrees of anisotropy of the curves remained mostly consistent between CTL and TIC subjects, overall behaving stiffer in the circumferential direction than in the radial direction (i.e., degree of anisotropy <1) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is supported by mechanical data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a significant 130% (p=0.006) increase in TIC anterior leaflet stiffness at large stretches (calf stiffness) in the radial direction.
source: However, our major finding from mechanical characterization was a significant 130% (p=0.006) increase in TIC anterior leaflet stiffness at large stretches (calf stiffness) in the radial direction. (Figure 5b).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by mechanical data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets had significantly increased circumferential stiffnesses at small stretches (toe stiffness) (p=0.008).
source: Additionally, we found that TIC anterior leaflets had significantly increased circumferential stiffnesses at small stretches (toe stiffness) (p=0.008, Figure 5c).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by mechanical data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: TIC anterior leaflets increased in stiffness predominantly in radial directions at higher stretches, and circumferential directions at lower stretches.
source: In summary, TIC anterior leaflets increased in stiffness. They increased predominantly in radial directions at higher stretches, and circumferential directions at lower stretches.
evidence: This summary is based on the mechanical testing data.

claim: Throughout the tissue depth, the mean collagen orientation remained mostly circumferential in CTL and TIC animals, with no apparent changes in mean direction among groups.
source: In our analysis, we found that throughout the tissue depth, the mean collagen orientation remained mostly circumferential in CTL and TIC animals, with no apparent changes in mean direction among groups (Figure 6a).
evidence: This finding is supported by two-photon microscopy data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: There was an increase in collagen fiber dispersion between CTL and TIC (indicated by a larger concentration parameter κ).
source: However, we noted an increase in collagen fiber dispersion between CTL and TIC (indicated by a larger concentration parameter κ).
evidence: This finding is supported by two-photon microscopy data shown in Figure 6.

claim: In TIC animals, more fibers were oriented in the radial direction than in the CTL subjects.
source: In other words, in TIC animals, more fibers were oriented in the radial direction than in the CTL subjects.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the increased fiber dispersion finding.

claim: There was a statistically significant increase in fiber dispersion in the 0–33% depth, nearest the atrialis, (p=0.017) in TIC subjects.
source: When separating our analysis into three depth regions we found a statistically significant increase in fiber dispersion in the 0–33% depth, nearest the atrialis, (p=0.017) in TIC subjects (Figure 6b).
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by regional two-photon microscopy data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Cell nuclei analyses for nuclear orientation, nuclear aspect ratio (NAR), and circularity showed no notable differences between CTL and TIC cell nuclei.
source: Similar analyses in cell nuclei for nuclear orientation, nuclear aspect ratio (NAR), and circularity showed no notable differences between CTL and TIC cell nuclei (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is supported by two-photon microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Collagen fibers in TIC anterior leaflets were more radially dispersed than CTL anterior leaflets near the atrialis.
source: In summary, we observed that collagen fibers in TIC anterior leaflets were more radially dispersed than CTL anterior leaflets near the atrialis.
evidence: This summary is based on two-photon microscopy data.

claim: The tricuspid valve, like the mitral valve, has a propensity to (mal)adapt.
source: We set out to identify whether the tricuspid valve, like the mitral valve, (mal)adapts. We provide significant evidence in support of the tricuspid valve's propensity to (mal)adapt on several scales.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the comprehensive experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The tricuspid valve (mal)adapts in a qualitatively very similar way to the mitral valve.
source: It does so in a qualitatively very similar way to the mitral valve.
evidence: This comparison is based on the similarity of findings to previous mitral valve studies.

claim: Similar tissue-level, matrix-level, and cell-level changes were found in the tricuspid valve as in the mitral valve.
source: Specifically, we found similar tissue-level, matrix-level, and cell-level changes.
evidence: This comparison is based on the multi-scale findings of the study.

claim: Strong evidence for EndoMT was not found in the tricuspid valve study.
source: The most significant difference being that we did not find strong evidence for EndoMT.
evidence: This is based on the absence of specific immunohistochemistry and proteomic findings.

claim: No CD31+ staining cells co-localized with αSMA were found, as reported in mitral valve studies.
source: Specifically, we did not find CD31+ staining cells co-localized with αSMA, as reported by Bartko et al., 2017.
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry findings and comparison to cited literature.

claim: No significant upregulation of proteins related to EndoMT was found in the proteomic analysis.
source: Similarly, we found no significant upregulation of proteins related to EndoMT in our proteomic analysis.
evidence: This is based on proteomic analysis findings.

claim: EndoMT may have occurred before or after the observational period in the study.
source: While the reasons could be multi-fold, one possible explanation could be that EndoMT may have occurred before or after our observational period.
evidence: This is speculation about why EndoMT was not observed.

claim: Losartan resulted in reduced mitral valve leaflet thickness, EndoMT, cellular activation, cell recruitment, and collagen deposition, while preserving leaflet area growth.
source: Specifically, the use of Losartan - an angiotensin II type one receptor antagonist that indirectly blocks the TGF-β1 phosphorylation of ERK in EndoMT (Wylie-Sears et al., 2014) - resulted in reduced mitral valve leaflet thickness, EndoMT, cellular activation, cell recruitment, and collagen deposition, while preserving leaflet area growth (Bartko et al., 2017).
evidence: This therapeutic finding in mitral valve is supported by citations.

claim: Surgical repair may initiate mitral valve tissue (mal)adaptation.
source: Interestingly, recent work has demonstrated that not only disease, but also surgical repair may initiate mitral valve tissue (mal)adaptation (Sielicka et al., 2018).
evidence: This finding about surgical effects is supported by a citation.

claim: The tricuspid valve may also (mal)adapt to repair.
source: It is possible that the tricuspid valve, may also (mal)adapt to repair.
evidence: This is speculation based on analogy to mitral valve findings.

claim: Promoting adaptive area increase of the valve could improve interventional efficacy by facilitating better leaflet coaptation.
source: For example, promoting adaptive area increase of the valve could improve interventional efficacy by facilitating better leaflet coaptation.
evidence: This is a speculative therapeutic implication based on the study findings.

claim: Avoiding maladaptive stiffening and thickening could prevent post-surgical repair failure.
source: Similarly, avoiding maladaptive stiffening and thickening could prevent post-surgical repair failure.
evidence: This is a speculative therapeutic implication based on the study findings.

claim: The tachycardia-induced biventricular heart failure model better represents the clinical setting of TR than a pulmonary hypertension model.
source: Regarding our animal model, we chose a tachycardia-induced biventricular heart failure model over a pulmonary hypertension model as it better represents the clinical setting of TR.
evidence: This is a justification for the experimental model choice based on clinical relevance.

claim: Few patients present with isolated TR.
source: That is, few patients present with isolated TR.
evidence: This is stated as clinical knowledge.

claim: 85–90% of severe TR cases are functional, resulting predominantly from left-sided heart disease.
source: In fact, 85–90% of severe TR cases are functional, resulting predominantly from left-sided heart disease (Mangieri et al., 2017).
evidence: This clinical statistic is supported by a citation.

claim: The ovine model demonstrates all salient features of biventricular disease such as reduced left and right ventricular ejection fraction, dilated ventricles, mitral and tricuspid annular dilation, and regurgitation in both valves.
source: Our model, with which we have years of experience, demonstrates all salient features of biventricular disease such as reduced left and right ventricular ejection fraction, dilated ventricles, mitral and tricuspid annular dilation, and regurgitation in both valves (Malinowski et al., 2017).
evidence: This characterization of the model is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The ovine model develops biventricular heart failure within weeks as opposed to years as in patients.
source: However, our ovine model develops biventricular heart failure within weeks as opposed to years as in patients.
evidence: This is a stated limitation of the model.

claim: The study is likely only reporting on the early response of the tricuspid leaflets to disease.
source: Thus, we are likely only reporting on the early response of the tricuspid leaflets to disease.
evidence: This is an inference based on the short time course of the model.

claim: The study focused only on the anterior leaflet, while the posterior and septal leaflets remain unreported on.
source: Finally, we focused our study only on the anterior leaflet, while the posterior and septal leaflets remain unreported on.
evidence: This is a stated limitation of the study scope.

claim: Recent publications highlight unique mechanical and microstructural properties between tricuspid valve leaflets.
source: With recent publications highlighting unique mechanical and microstructural properties between tricuspid valve leaflets (Meador et al., 2020a) as well as heterogeneous properties within leaflets, (Laurence et al., 2019; Kramer et al., 2019) we suggest that future studies investigate the heterogeneity of the (mal)adaptive response in the entire tricuspid valve.
evidence: This statement about leaflet heterogeneity is supported by citations.

claim: Pathological stimuli activate valvular interstitial cells, leading to changes in cellular phenotype and cell proliferation that emphasize inflammatory and profibrotic signaling pathways.
source: Specifically, we borrow from our understanding of the mitral valve and propose that, as pathological stimuli activate valvular interstitial cells, changes in cellular phenotype and cell proliferation likely emphasize inflammatory and profibrotic signaling pathways, which upregulate protein expression that initiates increased matrix turnover.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanistic model based on inference from the data and knowledge from mitral valve studies.

claim: Inflammatory and profibrotic signaling pathways upregulate protein expression that initiates increased matrix turnover.
source: Specifically, we borrow from our understanding of the mitral valve and propose that, as pathological stimuli activate valvular interstitial cells, changes in cellular phenotype and cell proliferation likely emphasize inflammatory and profibrotic signaling pathways, which upregulate protein expression that initiates increased matrix turnover.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanistic model based on inference from the data.

claim: Tissue-scale properties are dependent upon their micro-scale composition.
source: As tissue-scale properties are dependent upon their micro-scale composition, the tissue consequently exhibits altered morphological and mechanical properties as a direct result of cellularscale activity.
evidence: This is a general principle of tissue mechanics stated as established knowledge.

claim: The tissue exhibits altered morphological and mechanical properties as a direct result of cellular-scale activity.
source: As tissue-scale properties are dependent upon their micro-scale composition, the tissue consequently exhibits altered morphological and mechanical properties as a direct result of cellularscale activity.
evidence: This is an inference linking cellular changes to tissue-level changes based on the multi-scale data.

claim: Annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement in TIC animals respectively alter circumferential and radial strain.
source: These changes may be direct responses to annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement in TIC animals that respectively alter circumferential and radial strain.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanical stimuli causing the observed changes.

claim: Altered strain may disrupt the mechanobiological equilibrium in those directions, eliciting increased collagen deposition (radial) or degradation (circumferential) in an attempt to reestablish homeostasis.
source: In turn, altered strain may disrupt the mechanobiological equilibrium in those directions, eliciting increased collagen deposition (radial) or degradation (circumferential) in an attempt to reestablish homeostasis (Gupta and Grande-Allen, 2006).
evidence: This mechanobiological mechanism is proposed based on inference and supported by a citation.

claim: Radial stiffening may be an adaptive mechanism of the anterior leaflet.
source: Our stiffness results agree with our microstructural observations of increased collagen fiber dispersion in the radial direction and may suggest radial stiffening is an adaptive mechanism of the anterior leaflet.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of the observed stiffening.

claim: Elastin may play a role in remodeling, as it is often attributed with controlling the toe-region mechanical behavior of heart valve tissue.
source: Interestingly, we did observe a significantly stiffer circumferential toe region, which may suggest a role in remodeling for elastin, which is often attributed with controlling the toe-region mechanical behavior of heart valve tissue.
evidence: This is speculation based on the mechanical findings and established knowledge about elastin.

claim: Tissue thickness increase may be a direct consequence of upregulated collagen deposition.
source: Additionally, tissue thickness increase may be a direct consequence of upregulated collagen deposition.
evidence: This is an inference linking collagen increase to thickness increase.

claim: Thickness increase may also be due to inflammation-induced tissue swelling.
source: However, it cannot be ruled out that thickness increase may also be due to inflammation-induced tissue swelling.
evidence: This is an alternative speculation about the cause of thickness increase.

claim: Collagen increases were most prominent in the near-annulus and free edge regions.
source: Regionally, we observed that collagen increases were most prominent in the near-annulus and free edge regions.
evidence: This is based on regional collagen content data.

claim: Annular dilation and chordal tethering resulting from ventricular remodeling mechanically deformed the near-annulus and free edge regions of leaflet beyond normal physiological levels, inciting an increased profibrotic response by cells in these areas in an attempt to maintain mechanobiological homeostasis.
source: Considering the proximity of the near-annulus leaflet tissue to the annulus and the abundance of chordal attachments near the leaflet free edge, we propose that annular dilation and chordal tethering resulting from ventricular remodeling mechanically deformed these regions of leaflet beyond normal physiological levels, inciting an increased profibrotic response by cells in these areas in an attempt to maintain mechanobiological homeostasis (Gupta and Grande-Allen, 2006).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanistic explanation based on inference and supported by a citation.

claim: Altered shear stresses from regurgitant blood flow across the atrialis surface may have induced the observed microstructural adaptation.
source: Although this may be evidence of radial collagen deposition due to increased radial leaflet stresses from chordal tethering, it is also possible that altered shear stresses from regurgitant blood flow across the atrialis surface induced this microstructural adaptation.
evidence: This is an alternative speculation about the cause of collagen reorganization.

claim: Area increase measurements were taken in a mechanically stress-free state.
source: Importantly, as opposed to in vivo measurements of area increase that are taken under mechanical stress (due to chordal attachments, etc.), our measurements were taken in a mechanically stress-free state.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: Area increase is entirely due to growth as opposed to elastic stretch.
source: Thus, area increase is entirely due to growth as opposed to elastic stretch.
evidence: This is an inference based on the stress-free measurement conditions.

claim: Increased metabolic protein expressions may suggest increased energetic demands and a highly active response from valvular cells to TIC.
source: The increased metabolic protein expressions we observed may suggest increased energetic demands and a highly active response from valvular cells to TIC.
evidence: This is an inference from the proteomic data.

claim: Energy from increased metabolism may be necessary for the synthesis of apolipoproteins, serpins and complement proteins, and matrix proteins, which all increased in expression.
source: This energy may be necessary for the synthesis of apolipoproteins, serpins and complement proteins, and matrix proteins, which all increased in expression.
evidence: This is an inference linking metabolic changes to protein synthesis.

claim: Increases in expression levels of apolipoproteins, serpins, and complement proteins have been observed in calcific and stenotic aortic valves.
source: Increases in expression levels of such proteins have been observed in calcific (Novaro et al., 2003) and stenotic (O'Brien et al., 1996; Schlotter et al., 2018) aortic valves.
evidence: This comparison to other valve diseases is supported by citations.

claim: Increases in apolipoproteins, serpins, and complement proteins may lead to imbalances in lipid metabolism, increased inhibition of proteases such as antithrombins with consequent regulation of complement activation.
source: Such increases may lead to imbalances in lipid metabolism, increased inhibition of proteases such as antithrombins (Janciauskiene, 2001; Sanrattana et al., 2019) with consequent regulation of complement activation (Beinrohr et al., 2011; Chakraborti et al., 2000).
evidence: This mechanistic interpretation is supported by citations.

claim: Increased αSMA suggests a fibrotic response and matrix remodeling.
source: As a marker for valvular interstitial cell (VIC) activation, increased αSMA suggests a fibrotic response and matrix remodeling, (Liu et al., 2007) consistent with our findings of increased collagen content.
evidence: This interpretation is supported by a citation and consistency with other findings.

claim: Increased MMP13 highlights extracellular turn-over activity through collagenases.
source: Conjunctively, increased MMP13 highlights extracellular turn-over activity through collagenases.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the known function of MMP13.

claim: Further cellular recruitment from endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) processes is likely with increased TGF-β1, as TGF-β is a mediator of EndoMT and VIC activation in heart valves.
source: While an increased Ki67 expression indicates cellular proliferation, further cellular recruitment from endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) processes is likely with increased TGF-β1, as TGF-β is a mediator of EndoMT (Wylie-Sears et al., 2014) and VIC activation (Walker et al., 2004) in heart valves.
evidence: This inference is supported by citations about TGF-β function.

claim: Cellular density of tissues remained mostly similar despite evidence of cellular proliferation and recruitment, perhaps due to a balance by the increase in leaflet volume.
source: Despite evidence of cellular proliferation and recruitment, cellular density of our tissues remained mostly similar, perhaps due to a balance by the increase in leaflet volume (i.e., area and thickness increase) we observed.
evidence: This is an inference to explain the apparent contradiction between proliferation markers and cell density.

claim: Cell marker changes were regionally specific suggesting a heterogeneous cellular response, perhaps due to varying regional stimuli.
source: Furthermore, these cell marker changes were regionally specific suggesting a heterogeneous cellular response, perhaps due to varying regional stimuli.
evidence: This is an inference from the regional variation in marker expression.

claim: A total of 2457 proteins were confidently identified in the proteomic analysis.
source: With this, we confidently identified a total of 2457 proteins.
evidence: This describes the proteomic analysis results.

claim: The tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy ovine model has been previously described in detail and validated as a reliable and repeatable model of biventricular heart failure in sheep.
source: The tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy ovine model used in this study has been previously described in detail and validated as a reliable and repeatable model of biventricular heart failure in sheep (Malinowski et al., 2017).
evidence: This model validation is supported by a citation.

claim: Adult male Dorset sheep were randomly assigned to either control (CTL, n = 17, 59.9 ± 4.6 kg) or disease (TIC, n = 33, 60.1 ± 5.3 kg) groups.
source: In short, we randomly assigned adult male Dorset sheep to either control (CTL, n = 17, 59.9 ± 4.6 kg) or disease (TIC, n = 33, 60.1 ± 5.3 kg) groups.
evidence: This describes the experimental design and animal characteristics.
